sources.title: Laténium: Celtes, un millénaire d’images, exhibition booklet
sources.note: Printed page 6, full institutional indexed text read; direct PDF extraction failed. Hallstatt 800 to 450 BCE, La Tène 450 to 50 BCE, many peoples and changing alliances. The booklet’s broad non-writing characterization is not applied indiscriminately to later Gaulish inscriptions.

sources.title: Natural History Museum Vienna: The salt mine in prehistoric times
sources.note: Salt-rich, air-poor preservation of organic objects; incomplete archaeological sample from things lost, discarded or reused in mines.

sources.title: Natural History Museum Vienna: Everyday life underground in the Hallstatt Period
sources.note: Resource management, eating underground, Ritschert interpretation and other food remains. Contradictory statements about spoons/no cutlery and unsupported nutritional health claims are not adopted.

sources.title: Natural History Museum Vienna: Mining in the Hallstatt Period
sources.note: Children, lighting tapers, body lice, carrying and feces sections. Exact allocation of children’s jobs remains hypothetical; English page’s erroneous Stone Age wording for iron-age picks is not adopted.

sources.title: Karina Grömer, Natural History Museum Vienna: Quality of textiles
sources.note: Hallstatt-period thread dimensions, weave density, coloured patterns and spin direction. No oldest-ever textile claim is adopted.

sources.title: Natural History Museum Vienna: Technology used to produce textiles in Hallstatt
sources.note: Hand spindles, warp-weighted looms, Sopron image and tablet weaving. Modern reconstructions and ancient evidence are distinguished.

sources.title: Frank Maixner and colleagues: Hallstatt miners consumed blue cheese and beer, 2021
sources.note: Author-institution proof of Current Biology article, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2021.09.031. Printed pages 1, 6 and 9: sample 2604 fermented-food fungi, sample 2611 parasites. Four samples cover widely separated periods; findings are not a menu for every miner.

sources.title: Natural History Museum Vienna: Trade routes
sources.note: Support settlements, supply of food/clothes/tools, salt uses and routes following river valleys. Roman roads and equipment on the same page are not assigned to the Early Iron Age.

sources.title: Natural History Museum Vienna: Burial gifts from Hallstatt
sources.note: Name of cultural period, cremation and inhumation, imported goods and the preservation/collection bias in nineteenth-century excavation.

sources.title: Natural History Museum Vienna: Mass movements and their consequences
sources.note: Middle-fourth-century BCE debris flow and later Dammwiese mining continuation; local disaster is not an end to a pan-European people.

sources.title: Bibracte: La ville sous mes pieds
sources.note: Full institutional indexed text read after direct fetch failed. Côme-Chaudron workshops, Saint-Pierre spring and late Roman-style domus PC1. Medieval convent, nineteenth-century nursing customs and legends are excluded.

sources.title: Bibracte: Museum and archaeological visits
sources.note: Museum description: oppida appeared in the late second century BCE, Bibracte founded around 100 BCE and abandoned about a century later as Gaul became Roman. Visitor prices and modern activities are not historical evidence.

sources.title: Inrap: La Salmondière, Cesson-Sévigné
sources.note: L’époque gauloise section and captions for La Tène middle oval building and final-period four-post granary. Bronze Age house and glass bead, Roman forge and ambiguous combustion feature excluded.

sources.title: Bibracte: Démonstration de taille de meules, 25 April 2017
sources.note: Opening archaeological explanation of household hand mills for wheat flour; modern demonstration details not presented as ancient activity.

sources.title: British Museum: The Desborough Mirror, 1924,0109.1
sources.note: Full indexed object record read; direct retrieval failed. Broad date 50 BCE to 50 CE, three-part construction, polished front and engraved design; regional British form, not universal equipment.

sources.title: British Museum: The Battersea Shield, 1857,0715.1
sources.note: Collection record: bronze facing only, red glass studs, repoussé and hidden rivets, broad 350 to 50 BCE range. No unsupported ceremonial-only use or exact deposition date.

sources.title: Musée Alfred Danicourt, Joconde: Gold stater of Vercingetorix, 1887.A.108
sources.note: Historical context and description: 52 BCE attribution, VERCINGETOR[IX], running horse, crescent and amphora. Bracketed letters are explicitly editorial restoration; portrait identification is not assumed.

sources.title: Coline Ruiz Darasse, Scuola Normale Superiore: Sur les traces des Gaulois, 2020
sources.note: Seminar abstract dated 13 October 2020: Gaulish inscription corpus from the very end of the third century BCE to fourth century CE, France and adjacent regions. This does not certify universal literacy.

sources.title: Laténium: Annual report 2022
sources.note: Printed page 38, indexed full text: new gallery presents a reconstructed third-century BCE monument commemorating warrior values. Treated as archaeological interpretation, not a proven account of one particular battle.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Imported 400 to 323 BCE polygon spans -9.5491 to28.5681E and36.9903 to56.8897N. It is not a certified Hallstatt cultural distribution and postdates conventional800 to450BCE period. Public opening and period explicitly warn. Austrian mine examples are local, not universal customs of the entire polygon. No written witness established for cited miners; no false script supplied.

Imported700to500BCE record has one northernFrench polygon1.305to5.409E48.188to49.662N, predating conventional450to50BCE culture. Every narrative example is broader later context. Britain and Switzerland explicitly local; not within imported polygon. Desborough50BCEto50CE straddles period convention; labelled later. No link to a single successor state.
